Command routers load presentation and YAML, not the mode SKILL.md

Imply a command only when the mode registry records one

label: All 19 metadata-backed commands declare a choreography that loads a mode SKILL.md, and every named mode file exists.
The executing command routers do not load the mode SKILL.md; /create:skill and /deep:research load a presentation contract and auto or confirm YAML only.
The workflow YAML does not close the gap: create-skill-auto and deep-research-auto own their steps without loading the mode SKILL.md.
The 17 doctor commands have no command-metadata and do not load a mode skill; 11 carry a skill_agent owner tag but the routers resolve a target from _routes.yaml and load a target YAML.
/prompt:improve is the exception and explicitly loads the sk-prompt skill, the only non-hub command with an in-document skill load.
Nine skills have no dedicated command front door: cli-classifier, cli-external-orchestration, cli-orca, mcp-code-mode, mcp-tooling, sk-code, sk-git, system-skill-advisor and system-skilled-doctor.

A skill recommendation should imply a command only when the selected mode's registry entry records a command, as sk-doc and system-deep-loop do; a blanket implication would fabricate commands for nine skills.

Evidence against making the command primary: sk-doc marks its modes metadata-routed by hub membership and says a command-bridge mode is reached only via its command, never advisor-scored, so the command should sit beside the skill rather than replace it.
